summary: Mid-morning elevated 5xx wave: API gateway throttling amplifying upstream GPU soft-lock crashloops
description: Issue summary: BrightWrite reported a sustained spike of 5xx responses beginning ~08:45 local on 2026-03-12 for production traffic. Errors surface at the API gateway and are amplified by upstream runtime crashloops. Impact: multiple customer endpoints returned 502/503/504; customer-facing feature degraded for ~75% of requests during peak. Environment: Dedicated cluster in us-east, customer pinned to dedicated GPU pool. Timeline: 08:42 - first elevated latency ticks seen in metrics; 08:45 - customer reported 5xx rate >30% of requests; 08:50 - internal alert (error-rate) triggered; 09:10 - triage started. Customer reported increased request latency followed by steady 5xx floor.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Send production-like concurrent chat/embedding mix against customer's dedicated route (concurrency ~600).
2) Cold autoscaler warmup triggers (~08:30 pattern) followed by a wave of prefetched model loads.
3) Observe API gateway 429/502 spikes then persistent 5xx as runtimes hit GPU soft-locks.
4) Replaying same traffic on staging with identical load did not immediately reproduce until GPU driver probe introduced longer prefetch concurrency.
Notes: reproduction requires sustained mixed load and autoscaler warmup pattern (tenant-scale-up).
logs:
[2026-03-12T08:47:02Z] apigw: route=/v1/generate status=502 upstream_error='upstream reset' tenant=brightwrite
[2026-03-12T08:47:06Z] runtime: watchdog: nvml driver unresponsive, kernel signaled reset
[2026-03-12T08:47:09Z] runtime: pid=14321 exit_code=137 signal=9 reason='GPU driver soft-lock'
[2026-03-12T08:48:10Z] apigw: rate_limiter: token_bucket_drop tenant=brightwrite effective_rate=600r/s configured=500r/s
[2026-03-12T08:49:33Z] observability: trace_id=abc123 latency=1450ms alloc=2.1GB prefetch=1.2s
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: ingress rate limiter misconfiguration caused hedged retries and amplified connection churn. Secondary observation: serving-runtime instances experienced NVML/dGPU soft-locks under concurrent prefetch; driver log shows repeated resets and short-lived cuda contexts. Correlation: spikes in apigw token drops align with runtime restarts (pearson r=0.78 across 1-minute bins). Traces show high prefetch latency before crash. Autoscaler warmup created a cascading prefetch pressure: many runtimes initiated model loads simultaneously, increasing GPU context pressure and triggering driver soft-locks on particular kernel builds. We validated by isolating one runtime and reproducing higher error rate only when prefetch concurrency > 24. Metrics links: https://metrics.redwood.com/d/teams/brightwrite/5xx-waves and https://dash.redwood.com/runtimes/14321/events.
resolution: Workaround applied (2026-03-12 10:05): temporarily increased per-tenant token bucket and enabled conservative prefetch cap for BrightWrite (cap lowered to 8 concurrent prefetches). Routed traffic to fallback model variant (open-instruct-medium) while runtimes were restarted. Immediate effect: 5xx rate dropped below 2% within 12 minutes. Long-term fixes: (1) runtime PR#1987 (driver watchdog resilience) scheduled for canary 2026-03-15; (2) api-gateway PR#421 adjusts token-bucket calculation to account for warmup bursts and prevents hedged-retry amplification; (3) autoscaler backoff tuning to stagger shard prefetch; operational action items created: INT-55120 (autoscaler stagger job) and INT-55121 (driver vendor engagement for kernel-level fix). Customer notified of workaround and will be offered a credits review for impacted windows.
